notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I haven't written any notes on Joel 2.

My first try to load the commentary pages failed because of a mistake in my own code. When I tried again, I hit the limit on how many web requests I can make in one turn. No page was read: not Enduring Word, not Ellicott, Pulpit or Gill on biblehub, and not Precept Austin. I didn't get as far as the tradition-specific sites, NET Bible, or the Catholic and Orthodox sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything from memory.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start over. I'll load the pages one at a time so I don't hit the limit, and check each one loaded before moving on. I plan to work through these:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on biblehub/studylight, and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Two passages are likely to show real differences.
   - **Verses 28–32:** Peter quotes this passage in Acts 2. I'll look at what each tradition's own teachers say:
     - Pentecostal: ag.org, Sam Storms, Pneuma Review
     - Reformed: Ligonier, TGC, Monergism
     - Baptist: Desiring God, GTY, Spurgeon
     - Wesleyan: Wesley's notes, Seedbed
     - Lutheran: LCMS, 1517
   - **Verses 1–11:** whether the "army" is the locusts of chapter 1 or a human invader.
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship
   - New Advent (the Church Fathers), Catholic Answers and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings
   - Any critiques the sites publish of popular teaching on verse 25 ("I will repay you for the years") or on the outpouring of the Spirit

If you'd rather go faster, you could split the job across messages, for example verses 1–17 first, then 18–27, then 28–32.
